first_impression.reaction: Arrived from a Google search for 'wedding morning timeline'. The first paragraph actually answers the question with a worked example: 'For a 4pm ceremony, for example, that can mean hair and makeup from 9am with a first look or from 10am without one.' No 'dream day' preamble, so I kept going. It's a bit early for us (no destination yet, 14 months out), but this is the kind of thing I'd forward to my sister and future bridesmaids.

journey.quote: A wedding morning timeline is built backwards from the ceremony: fix the time you leave, then the time you must be dressed, then when the photographer arrives, and start the first hair and makeup chair early enough to finish everyone before that.
journey.reaction: A clear method I can apply myself. That's the kind of logic I trust.

journey.section: How long bridal hair and makeup takes
journey.quote: There is no single honest figure to plan around.
journey.reaction: I like that they don't make up a number. I'd rather hear 'get it in writing from your artist' than a made-up 45 minutes.

journey.section: Stylists and artists for the number of people
journey.quote: If their answer starts earlier than anyone would like, the choice is an earlier start, or a second stylist or artist so more chairs run at once.
journey.reaction: An honest trade-off, put plainly. Useful.

journey.section: A sample wedding morning timeline for a 4pm ceremony
journey.quote: Every time is an example to adapt, not a rule.
journey.reaction: Fine, but I can't tell how many people the 9am start is for. Two of us plus four bridesmaids? Plus mums? I had to go back up the page to work out that the headcount is what moves it.

journey.quote: Away from home, more of the morning belongs to the venue.
journey.reaction: This is the bit that's actually relevant to us. The questions about suite access, the walk in a long gown and humidity feel like insider knowledge, not filler.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world and is your single point of contact from start to finish, so questions like these go to one person.
journey.reaction: Every planner says 'single point of contact from start to finish'. It reads like the stock line. Tie it to the questions just above it and it lands better.

journey.section: When the ceremony is in the morning
journey.quote: Move the ceremony to 11am with the same people and team, and that chair moves to 4.30am.
journey.reaction: Ha, that's a great reality check. I'd show James this one.

journey.section: A wedding morning schedule template to copy
journey.quote: Copy this into a document or spreadsheet and fill it from the bottom up, starting with the ceremony.
journey.reaction: Practical and shareable. Though honestly, a spreadsheet is the thing we're trying to avoid doing ourselves for 18 months.

journey.section: Plan the morning with one person
journey.quote: Plan the morning with one person
journey.reaction: That heading made me wonder whether the Advisor is actually there in the suite with us on the morning. The body doesn't say that, so the heading slightly over-promises or at least confuses.

journey.section: Plan the morning with one person
journey.quote: a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: Fee and inclusions in writing up front speaks straight to my worry about hidden costs. Good, but still no idea of a range.

unanswered_questions: How many people in the chairs do the 4pm example times assume?
What does working with a Wedded Advisor cost, even as a range?
On the wedding morning abroad, who is accountable if the stylist is late or the suite isn't ready?
Is there a real wedding (venue and date) where this kind of morning was planned, so we can see it in practice?
Does the Advisor help us find and brief a hair and makeup team at the destination, or do we source them ourselves?
would_share_with: Maid of honour and bridesmaids, for the template
Mum, since she'd want to know when she sits in the chair

cta_reaction.quote: If you would like to plan it with someone, a Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, agrees the fee in writing before any work begins, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
cta_reaction.why: It's low pressure and the fee-in-writing line helps. But I enquire after a couple of posts plus a real wedding, and this post alone doesn't show me what 'end to end' means in practice. I'd probably click through to see what Concierge is, not enquire yet.

top_3_changes: Replace heading "## Plan the morning with one person" with "## Work back from the ceremony" so it doesn't read as though the Advisor is with us on the morning.

Replace "Every time is an example to adapt, not a rule." with "Every time is an example to adapt, not a rule: your own start depends on how many people are in the chairs and the pace your stylist and artist give you."

Replace "so questions like these go to one person." with "so questions like these about the suite, the walk and the light go to one person rather than to the venue, the stylist and the photographer separately."

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Sophie & James (early research, Sydney, destination wedding)
No invented brand facts; unknowns listed in unanswered_questions

Suggested edits are exact old/new strings and add no prices, statistics, durations, vendor names, fees, on-the-ground staffing, transfers, availability or implication that the Advisor runs the morning
VERIFY markers and HTML comments treated as invisible
No problems invented; no turn-offs found so none listed

open_questions.question: Persona is provisional (not CRM-calibrated); should the low enquiry score for a how-to post at early research stage be weighted down?
Is a real wedding link available to add near the Concierge CTA? This persona enquires only after seeing one.
